explanation: Array.prototype.sort() with no comparator function converts every element to a string and compares them lexicographically (by UTF-16 code unit), not numerically. So for [10, 9, 2, 21], the elements become the strings "10", "9", "2", "21", and since '1' < '2' < '9' character-wise, the result is [10, 2, 21, 9] instead of the numerically sorted [2, 9, 10, 21]. Fixing it requires an explicit comparator like `(a, b) => a - b`.
prompt: Why does this function fail to produce a numerically sorted list of scores?
choices: Array.prototype.sort() with no comparator converts elements to strings and sorts lexicographically, so multi-digit numbers end up out of numeric order
sort() mutates the original array instead of returning a new one, so the scores are lost after the call
The function should use a for loop instead of sort() to handle numeric arrays
sort() only works on arrays of strings, so passing numbers throws a TypeError
